append.row: | *Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me* (6:2 = 37:2
append.text: **Ps 37:2 copies it exactly** (D21); passed the Latinist twice. The Introit verse of Quad2-3 sings it (grep).
**Ps 37:3 *sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi* → *as vossas setas ficaram cravadas em mim*** — the row held at the place it named; passed the Latinist twice and every reader.

**Ps 37:3 and 37:20 *confirmásti super me manum tuam … confirmáti sunt super me* → *firmastes sobre mim a vossa mão … se firmaram sobre mim*** — the row's option *firmar*, one verb for the psalm's echo (*confirmastes a mão* would be heard as attesting, as 36:17). The gate Latinist asked the passive *foram fortalecidos* (minor), refused for the echo; the blind reader heard 'gained the upper hand'. Evidence for a split: with a thing or a hand pressed upon someone → *firmar*.
**Ps 37:11 *derelíquit me virtus mea* → *abandonou-me o meu vigor*** — the proposal *vigor* applied at a place it named; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.

**Ps 37:12 *Amíci mei, et próximi mei ** → *Os meus amigos e os meus próximos ** — the one place where the proparoxytone stands at the mediant: draft 1's postposed *Os amigos meus e os próximos meus* (to save the cadence) was refused by the stylist as calqued and precious; the plain order won (D2: the ear leads on order). His *vizinhos* refused (vicínus's; and *próximos … aproximaram* echoes *próximi … appropinquavérunt*).

**Ps 37:12, 12b *appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt … de longe stetérunt* → *e ficaram de pé … ficaram de longe*** (the Latinist's v1 fix): draft 1 *se detiveram* (1:1's *deter-se*) was marked minor twice, heard by the blind reader as 'were detained', and *se detiveram de longe* was unidiomatic to the stylist. So *deter-se* only for halting on a road (1:1).

**Ps 37:17 in quoted speech — *Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei* → *Porque eu disse: Que os meus inimigos não se alegrem à minha custa*** (draft 2): draft 1 *Para que não se alegrem* was heard by the blind reader as a purpose clause ('I said this so that…') and was the stylist's worst line. After a verb of saying the quoted words are a wish: *Que … não* + subjunctive. *para que não* stays where the clause depends on a verb (2:12, 27:1). The gate Latinist asked *nunca* for the *quando* (minor, refused; option).

Ps 37:17 *supergáudeant mihi* → *se alegrem à minha custa* — the family's third place, applied. The Latinist asked *exultem sobre mim* twice (minor), the stylist once — refused (*exultar* is exsultáre's); the blind reader heard gloating first.

**Ps 37:13 *locúti sunt vanitátes* → *falaram vaidades*:** the stylist heard pride and asked *coisas vãs*; the blind reader listed this sense unknown and heard boasting. Kept for the row (*coisas vãs* is inánia / vana's, 2:1, 11:3) — but the row's word has now been heard as conceit by readers in Pss 4/118, 30 and 37: **for the coordinator**: *o que é vão* / *coisas vazias* are the candidates that collide with nothing.

Ps 37:13 *dolos tota die meditabántur* → *e o dia todo meditavam enganos*: the stylist heard *meditar* as devotional and asked *tramavam* — refused (the Latin's one verb for the just man and the plotter); the blind reader heard 'thought up deceptions' first.
Ps 37:7 *curvátus sum usque in finem* → *fiquei curvado até o fim* (as 15:11, *usque in finem*); the blind reader heard it temporal ('until the end'); DRB 'even to the end'. Kept.
Ps 37:6 *a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ* → *diante da minha insensatez* (the noun, as the row names); the blind reader listed *insensatez* unknown; kept.

**Ps 37:4 ×2, 37:6 — *a fácie* of a cause (ἀπὸ προσώπου: *a fácie iræ tuæ … peccatórum meórum … insipiéntiæ meæ*) → *diante de*** (*diante da vossa ira*): *da face de* is not Portuguese there; *diante de* keeps both senses (because of / in the presence of). The Latinist passed it twice; the blind reader heard 'in front of', not cause. *por causa de* (DRB, MS1932) is option 1 in Ps 37's decision `afacie`.

terms: | illúsio | escárnio (*os meus lombos estão cheios de escárnios*) | open | Ps 37:8; 78:4 *subsannátio et illúsio* the other place (grep). ἐμπαιγμός, mockery. Draft 1 had the cognate *ilusões* (DRB, MS1932, and L&S's 'eccl.' sense citing this verse): **the Latinist marked it MAJOR**, the stylist and the blind reader heard fantasies. *escárnio* is of the family the derídere row gives *escarnecer* (21:8); derísum (43:14 *subsannatiónem et derísum*) is the near twin of 78:4 — they never meet in a verse, but the coordinator may want to keep them apart (*zombaria* is subsannáre's). Option *ilusões* kept in Ps 37. |

| lumbi | lombos | open | Ps 37:8 (ψύαι), only place in the psalms (grep). The organ named (rule 5), apart from renes → *rins*. The blind reader listed *lombos* unknown and heard the lower back; the Latinist and stylist passed it. Option *entranhas* (MS1932). |
| sánitas | saúde (*não há saúde na minha carne*) | working | Ps 37:4 = 37:8b, the only places (grep). ἴασις. Heard as bodily health. MS1932 *parte sã* is the option. |

| cicatrix | cicatriz | open | Ps 37:6, only place. The Latin's word (L&S 'a scar'); DRB *sores*, MS1932 *chagas* make open wounds. The blind reader found rotting scars puzzling; the Latinist passed it twice. Option *chagas*. |

| supergrédi | ultrapassar (*as minhas iniquidades ultrapassaram a minha cabeça*) | working | Ps 37:5, only place. The blind reader heard 'more than I can bear'. *se elevaram acima da* (MS1932, the Greek) the option. |

| redargútio | repreensão (*e que não tem repreensões na sua boca*) | open | Ps 37:15, only place (grep); ἐλεγμοί — the noun of ἐλέγχω, which is árguere → *repreender* in 37:2, so the echo is kept. The stylist asked *réplicas* (plainer; refused, option); the blind reader heard 'does not scold others'. |

| detráhere + dative | difamar (*me difamavam*) | open | Ps 37:21; 70:13 *detrahéntes ánimæ meæ*, 100:5, 108:4, 108:20, 108:29 (grep, 6 lines). ἐνδιέβαλλον, slandered. *caluniar* is calumniári's. Passed all readers. Options *falar mal de*, *murmurar de* (MS1932). |

| magna loqui (*super me*) | falar grandezas (contra mim) | open | 11:4 *magníloquam* → *que fala grandezas*, 34:26b, 37:17, 54:13 (grep). **Ps 37:17: the stylist asked *grandes coisas* ('grandezas suggests quantities or splendours') and the blind reader listed *grandezas* (as boasts) unknown** — kept for 11:4 and 34:26b; if it changes, the three change together. |
formulas: | *Inténde in adjutórium meum* (37:23; 69:2 *Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde*, which opens every Hour; the Matins antiphon *Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ*, Psalmi matutinum; Introit of Quad2-3 — grep) | *Atendei em meu auxílio* | open — Ps 37: D3's *atender* with the phrase *em meu auxílio*. The stylist called *atender em* not Portuguese and asked *Acudi em meu auxílio*; the blind reader heard 'come to my help' first; the Latinist passed it twice. **For the coordinator before Ps 69**: the versicle of every Hour will say whatever is ruled here. |

| *Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: * ne discésseris a me* (37:22; the Introit of Quad2-3; 21:11b *ne discésseris a me*) | *Não me abandoneis, Senhor, meu Deus: * não vos afasteis de mim* | working — Ps 37 (second colon copied from 21:11) |
